defects.claim: A non-finite legacy polygon sides or star points count reaches the builder unvalidated and its vertex loop never ends, stalling painting
defects.scenario: a node `{ shape: 'polygon', sides: 1e9 }` (from JSON, a property panel, or a slider) → `regularPolygonPath` loops 1e9 times inside paint, silhouette and drawnBounds, which hangs the frame. `sides: 2.5` draws an uneven three-point outline (angles at i/2.5). `sides: 0` or a negative value gives an empty path. `points` for a star behaves the same way. `shapeGenerator.ts` answers the same question ("what count does a polygon/star get") with `clampShapeGenerator` → `count()` = `clamp(Math.round(v), SHAPE_COUNT_RANGE)`. The painter should go through that same clamp.
defects.cause: count clamp not shared; two pathways for one decision

defects.claim: Bounds ignore animated trim, so a square-capped smooth shape's cap overhang falls outside the reported drawn box
strokedBounds includes the stroke ribbon for a stroke with no paint that only draws marker heads, overstating bounds
defects.scenario: a path-posed node, a derived node, or a `kit:shape` node with a marker has `data.stroke = { width: 20, markerEnd: { key: 'arrow', size: 4 } }` and no `paint`. `resolveStroke` keeps it because it carries a marker, and `commandStroke` passes it to the renderer with no paint, so only the arrow head is drawn. `strokedBounds` never looks at `stroke.paint`. When `align !== 'inner'` it always tessellates the full ribbon at width 20, with miter joins, and adds every ribbon vertex to the box. So `drawnBounds` (from `PATH_POSE_PAINTER.drawnBounds`, `derivedDrawnBounds`, and `SHAPE_PAINTER.drawnBounds` through `strokedPoseBox`, since a marker makes `protrudes` true) comes out 10 units wider than the path on every side. At a sharp corner the miter adds up to `miterLimit * 10` more. None of that area is painted, so selection chrome, alignment and fit-to-content sit on a box larger than what is drawn. `inkReach` in nodePaint.ts handles the same case another way: `const line = stroke.paint == null ? 0 : 1`, so the line has no reach and only the heads do. The two places disagree on whether a stroke with no paint inks its line. The fix: when `stroke.paint == null`, skip the ribbon and keep only the marker heads.
defects.cause: the stroke's paint is not checked before the ribbon is tessellated

defects.claim: A group's box border bounds use a uniform outset, disagreeing with kit:shape's measurement of the same rect when its stroke protrudes
FRAMED pick cache keyed on pose identity picks against a stale outline when a pose buffer is mutated in place
defects.scenario: a derived node built from `pathFromParts` has its pose animated by a per-frame override that writes into one pose buffer in place. `dropPoseKeyedMemoSlots` exists for exactly this case and clears nodeMemo's pose-keyed slots. But `FRAMED` is a module WeakMap outside nodeMemo. While the derived path is unchanged, `hit.pose === pose` stays true, so `partsCover` hit-tests the part's outline framed by the pose as it stood on the first pick. A pick then lands on the old position or rotation instead of the drawn one. Should go through nodeMemo, or compare the pose by value.
defects.cause: identity cache key on a buffer that is mutated in place

defects.claim: hasStroke duplicates strokeHasInk but omits its non-finite-dash test, so the two disagree on whether a stroke with a non-finite dash draws ink
defects.scenario: a node stroked `{ paint: {color:'#000'}, width: 2, dash: [Infinity, 1] }` (or any dash `dashPattern` calls `'non-finite'`). The renderer and pdf draw no line for it, and `@weasel-js/paint`'s `strokeHasInk` (paintKey.ts:71) answers false; `hasStroke` answers true, so path-tools' Outline Stroke (`outlineStrokeAction.tsx:39`) and text-tools' `textOutline.ts:15` treat the node as stroked and offer to outline a line that is not drawn. Same question, two definitions; `hasStroke` should be `strokeHasInk`.
defects.cause: duplicated predicate drifted from its paint-package original

defects.claim: A rect's or ellipse's drawn bounds grow every side by the widest per-vertex stroke width, not the width at each side
defects.scenario: `shape: 'rect'` with `stroke.vertexWidths: [1, 1, 40, 1]`. `protrudes` is false, so `outsetPoseBox` is used, and it takes `inkReach`'s `widestStrokeWidth` (40) as an even outset on all four sides. The ribbon is only wide near one corner, yet the selection chrome stands 20 units off every edge. `drawnBounds` is documented as tight ("Not conservative, unlike `bounds`"). Per-vertex widths should send it through `strokedPoseBox`, as polygons and stars already go.

defects.claim: hasStroke and inkReach disagree on whether a stroke width has ink
defects.scenario: a stroke with `width: Infinity` (or `{ px: Infinity }`). `hasStroke` tests only `> 0` and returns true, so an outline action treats the stroke as having ink to outline. `inkReach` uses `widthHasInk` (`> 0 && finite`) and reports no reach, and the renderer draws nothing. The fix is to use `widthHasInk` in `hasStroke` as well.

defects.claim: kit:path-pose re-tessellates the stroke on every drawnBounds call
defects.scenario: snapping reads `drawnBounds` for candidate nodes on every pointer move (frames.ts `drawnBounds`, "what a snap … measures"). `kit:path` and `kit:shape` memoize this through `strokedPoseBox`, so "a drag that only moves the node does not stroke it again". `kit:path-pose` and `kit:derived` call `strokedBounds` directly with no memo, so every pointer move re-tessellates every such node's full stroke, dashes and markers included. Cost grows with node count × path size on each move.
defects.cause: stroked-bounds memo applied on one path only

defects.claim: kit:derived re-tessellates the stroke on every drawnBounds call
defects.scenario: snapping reads `drawnBounds` for candidate nodes on every pointer move (frames.ts `drawnBounds`, "what a snap … measures"). `kit:path` and `kit:shape` memoize this through `strokedPoseBox`, so "a drag that only moves the node does not stroke it again". `kit:path-pose` and `kit:derived` call `strokedBounds` directly with no memo, so every pointer move re-tessellates every such node's full stroke, dashes and markers included. Cost grows with node count × path size on each move.
defects.cause: stroked-bounds memo applied on one path only

defects.claim: A paint-less marked stroke's invisible line is grabbable by pick at the head's reach, because inkReach counts the line as ink.
defects.scenario: same stroke as above, head reach R. `sides(full, headReach)` gives `outset = headReach` even with `line = 0`, and `inkCovers` applies `outset` along the entire outline (`strokeHitTest(path, …, reach)`), so a click anywhere within R of the undrawn line picks the node, though only the heads are visible. The comment beside it says the line "reaches nowhere".
defects.cause: head reach folded into a per-outline reach

defects.claim: kit:derived's ink reads the node's own paint for a path drawn in parts, so the pick index and area select disagree with what the parts paint
defects.scenario: a derived node made by `pathFromParts` whose own `data.stroke` is null and `data.fill` null, with a part stroked 20 wide and another part filled. `paint` and `partsCover` use each part's paint (`resolvePartPaint`), but `ink` reports `filled: false, outset: 0`. `nodeBroadBox` (pickIndex/nodeBroadBox.ts:68) grows the broad box by that 0 outset, so a click 8 units outside the path on the 20-wide part's stroke is culled by the index before `partsCover` (which would accept it) ever runs. `hitTestArea` (deps/hitTestArea.ts:163) reads `filled` from the same `ink`, so a marquee in `intersects` mode drawn wholly inside a filled part treats the node as an unfilled outline and misses it. Should: for a parts path, `ink` reports the union over parts (filled if any part fills, outset/inset/outsetPx the max of each part's `inkReach`).
defects.cause: ink ignores derivedPartsOf where paint/pick/drawnBounds honor it

defects.claim: outsetPoseBox under-outsets a mitered { px } rect under a skewed screen map, so the drawn bounds fall short of the stroke.
defects.scenario: a `shape: 'rect'` node (or a group box border) with `stroke: { width: { px: 10 }, join: 'miter' }`, viewed through a `ctx.screen` map that has shear (a skewed pose frame). The renderer builds the `{ px }` ribbon on screen, where the rect's corners are no longer right angles. At the acute corners the miter spikes reach past the disk-support outset that `strokeOutsetPerAxis` adds, by up to `miterLimit × w/2`. The "exact for a rect" claim holds only when the map keeps angles. Expected: under a non-conformal map, route the rect through `strokedPoseBox` the way polygon and star are routed.
defects.cause: right-angle assumption broken by a shearing screen map

defects.claim: strokedBounds pads an absolute path's drawn box by 2^-16 of its distance from the origin, which is far coarser than float32 precision
defects.scenario: `FINEST = 2 ** -16` is applied to `size`, which is the largest absolute coordinate, so it measures distance from the origin, not the path's extent. float32 resolves 2^-24 of a coordinate, so this is 256× coarser than the comment says. `PATH_POSE_PAINTER.drawnBounds` and `derivedDrawnBounds` pass absolute paths. Example: a 100-unit path-posed ellipse at x = 1e5, viewed at zoom 10, has a view tolerance of 0.05 and finest = 1.53. So `flattenFor` returns `pad: 1.53`, and every ribbon vertex grows the box by 1.53 world units on each side. The selection chrome then sits about 15 px off the stroke. At x = 1e6 it is 15 world units, which is 150 px at zoom 10. It should stay tight to about the renderer's own tolerance. (`strokedPoseBox` is unaffected because it strokes at the origin.)
defects.cause: precision floor scaled by distance from origin at 2^-16 instead of float32's 2^-24 (or the path's own extent)

defects.claim: kit:shape draws data.sides/points unrounded and unclamped, so its path disagrees with the shape generator's counts
defects.scenario: a JSON scene node `{ shape: 'polygon', sides: 5.5 }` paints a 6-vertex outline whose last edge is short (angles `i / 5.5 · 2π`), not a regular polygon; `sides: 0`, a negative count or `NaN` paints an empty closed path; `sides: 1e8` allocates 1e8 vertices on every paint, silhouette and drawn-bounds call; `sides: Infinity` never leaves `regularPolygonPath`'s loop (packages/geom/src/paths/builder.ts:261), hanging the frame. Same for `points` through `starPath`. `shapeGeneratorPath` answers the same question with `count()` = round and clamp to `SHAPE_COUNT_RANGE` (3..32) (packages/core/src/domains/paths/shapeGenerator.ts:74), so the two pathways draw different shapes for one count.

defects.claim: strokedBounds tessellates an infinite stroke width instead of returning null
defects.scenario: a stroke whose resolved width is `Infinity` passes `!(width > 0)` and is tessellated at infinite width; the box comes back with infinite or NaN extents (Infinity − Infinity), so `drawnBounds` of a node the renderer draws no line for (`widthHasInk` false) is infinite/NaN, poisoning a union of drawn bounds (fit-to-content, export box). Should be `!widthHasInk(width)` → no ribbon, as `inkReach` decides.

defects.claim: A group's drawn bounds omit the marker heads on its border.
defects.scenario: a group with `data.border = { paint, width: 2, markerMid: 'dot' }` (or a marker-only border, which `resolveStroke` keeps and `paintGroupBox` strokes via `commandStroke`) paints heads at the box corners, but `groupBoxDrawnBounds` always uses `outsetPoseBox`, the uniform stroke outset. `SHAPE_PAINTER.drawnBounds` decides the same rect case through `protrudes()` and measures with `strokedPoseBox` when a marker is present, so a stroked rect node and a bordered group with the same stroke report different drawn boxes; the group's is too small by the heads' reach.
defects.cause: protrusion rule applied in shape painter only

defects.claim: hasStroke reports an infinite-width stroke as drawn, though the renderer refuses to draw it.
defects.scenario: `hasStroke({ paint, width: Infinity })` (or `{ px: Infinity }`) returns true, so Outline Stroke (path-tools outlineStrokeAction.tsx:39) is offered and text-tools reports the node stroked, while `inkReach` uses `widthHasInk` (positive *and finite*) and reports no ink, and the tessellator draws nothing. Two answers to "does this stroke have ink"; `hasStroke` should use `widthHasInk`.

defects.claim: A polygon or star on a mirrored pose is drawn unmirrored
defects.scenario: a `shape: 'polygon', sides: 3` node resized past its opposite edge gets a negative `width` (or `height`). `pathForShape` centers the polygon and takes `Math.abs` for the radius, so the triangle keeps pointing the same way, while the rect and `kit:path` (via `pathInPoseBox`) mirror with the pose and the fill's box-relative gradient (`commandFill(declaredFill, pose)`) is baked onto the mirrored box. The shape and its gradient flip relative to each other.
